walkthroughs.body_html:
Physical Chemistry — a core area of A-Level Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Physical Chemistry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Physical Chemistry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: In pV = nRT with p in Pa and V in m³, the gas constant R is:
options: 8.31 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹
96 500 C mol⁻¹
6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹

mcqs.q: Breaking a chemical bond is always:
options: Endothermic
Exothermic
Energy-neutral
Spontaneous

mcqs.q: Which change alters the value of Kc?
options: Changing the temperature
Adding more reactant
Increasing the pressure
Adding a catalyst

mcqs.q: Increasing the pressure on N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ shifts the equilibrium:
options: Right, towards fewer gas moles
Left, towards more gas moles
It has no effect
It stops the reaction

mcqs.q: Does Kc change when more reactant is added at constant temperature?
options: Adding reactant always halves the value of Kc.
No — Kc is fixed at a given temperature; the concentrations adjust until the same equilibrium ratio is restored.
At equilibrium only the reverse reaction keeps going.
Adding reactant increases Kc because more product is formed.

mcqs.q: At equilibrium, have the forward and reverse reactions stopped?
options: Bond enthalpies apply only to ionic compounds.
At equilibrium the reaction has finished and nothing is happening.
No — both continue at equal rates, so concentrations stay constant; the equilibrium is dynamic.
At equilibrium only the reverse reaction keeps going.

mcqs.q: Are mean bond enthalpies exact for every molecule?
options: Bond enthalpy calculations give the exact ΔH for any reaction.
Bond enthalpies apply only to ionic compounds.
No — they are averages over many compounds, so ΔH values calculated from them are only approximate.
At equilibrium only the reverse reaction keeps going.
